newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle and feeder cattle close easier.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle and feeder cattle close easier.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed lower paced by live cattle following further weakness in boxed beef and concern over larger fed cattle supplies ahead. Feeder cattle followed in light trade, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.725 to 0.350 cent per lb lower with June off most at 63.925 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.300 to 0.075 lower with May off 0.150 at 72.250 cents. April expired earlier at 72.425, off 0.025 cent.
Concern was growing that declining boxed beef values would encourage packers to reduce recent active slaughter rate and reduce further their bids for fed cattle, traders said.

Adding to overall pressure were expectations of increased fed cattle supplies going into the summer months. Previous cattle-on-feed reports indicated increased placements that will be available starting in June, they said.

"June futures at this juncture, and even the August, have to reconcile with the fact that we still have a fairly significant supply of animals in the feedlots that are going to be coming to market over the next few months," said Dale Durchholz, market analyst for AgriVisor Services Inc.
Seasonally, beef demand also sags after the Memorial Day holiday, Durchholz added.

Cargill Investor Services sold June while R.J. O'Brien bought. Refco and Cargill bought August while R.J. O'Brien sold. Stone Traders bought August and sold June and October on spreads, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses sold June 62 puts and bought June 60 puts. Commercials bought December 68 puts and sold 74 calls, pit sources added.

Feeders followed the lead of live cattle most of the day and moved lower despite lower corn futures. Profit taking also offset the recent strength in cash feeders and a 26-month high in the latest CME feeder cattle index, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.01 at $72.15 per cwt. The previous quote of $72.16 was the highest price level since February 22, 1995.
Cargill sold May against long spreads in February live cattle while LIT division of First Options bought May. Lind-Waldock notably sold May early. Refco sold August, pit sources added.
